findings.rationale: Replay only checks that a domain event or effect name is declared. Domain events are added to `observed`, and effect requests are added to `pending`, without verifying that the monitor's preceding transition emitted or authorized them. A log containing an impossible declared event—or an unauthorized external-effect request—can therefore be reported as `conformance_checked`, undermining the runtime-conformance boundary.

Every effect request is inserted into a set without checking the insertion result, so repeated requests with the same correlation are silently collapsed even though the external irreversible operation may have run twice. The later at-most-once check occurs only at completion and keys solely on correlation rather than the effect's declared `idempotency_key`; retries using a new correlation can bypass it as well.
